subtitle: A meal in a mango grove, a hall of citizens, and the last walk of a teacher

panels.shot: wide, dusk panorama of a small republican town with an assembly hall and a serene mendicant walking toward a mango grove where a humble blacksmith waits
panels.action: Cunda of Pava, in simple worker’s clothes, stands at the edge of his mango grove, hands folded, watching a calm wandering Teacher approach as the silhouette of the Malla assembly hall rises behind the town.

dialogue.text: In the fading light at Pava, a blacksmith’s meal, a new Malla hall, and the Buddha’s last journey crossed paths—leaving a small republic etched forever in a great religious memory.

i18n.hi: ढलती रोशनी में पावा, लोहार का भोजन, नया मल्ल सभा भवन, और बुद्ध की अंतिम यात्रा टकरा पड़ीं—और एक नन्हा गणराज्य हमेशा के लिए महान धर्मकथा में दर्ज हो गया।

panels.shot: slow aerial sweep over the Ganges plain, then descending toward clustered towns and groves
panels.action: An expansive view of the 5th-century BCE Ganges plain shows scattered fortified towns, winding roads, and patches of mango groves under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: In the age of mahajanapadas, great kingdoms bestrode the Ganges plain. Yet between their crowns, small republics like the Mallas held their ground with councils, halls, and stubborn pride.

i18n.hi: महाजनपदों के युग में गंगा के मैदान पर बड़े राज खड़े थे। पर उनके बीच, मल्ल जैसे छोटे गण अपने सभा भवनों, परिषदों और अड़ियल गौरव से डटे रहे।

panels.shot: medium-wide shot of a modest republican town with defensive ditch and wooden palisade
panels.action: The town of Pava appears as a compact settlement with timber palisades, a gatehouse, and earthen streets where traders, farmers, and craftsmen move among simple houses.

dialogue.text: Pava, in the land of the Mallas, was one such town—no royal palace, no king’s throne. Its strength lay in its people, its clan assembly, its shared decisions in a santhagara, an assembly hall.

i18n.hi: मल्ल देश का पावा भी ऐसा ही नगर था—न राजमहल, न राजा का सिंहासन। उसकी ताकत थी उसके लोग, उसकी कुल-सभा, और संथागार नाम का साझा सभा भवन।

panels.shot: close-up on hands at a forge, sparks flying, with face half-lit by the fire
panels.action: Cunda of Pava stands at his forge, sweat on his brow, hammer raised above glowing metal as sparks leap against the dark interior of a simple workshop.

dialogue.text: Among Pava’s kammara, the metalworkers, was Cunda. His hands shaped ploughshares and tools, iron that bound the town’s daily life together.

i18n.hi: पावा के कम्मार, यानी धातुकारों में, कुंडा भी था। उसके हाथ हल की नोक और औज़ार गढ़ते, लोहे से नगर की रोज़मर्रा की रगड़-जगड़ को जोड़ते।

panels.shot: wide shot of Cunda’s mango grove on the edge of town
panels.action: Cunda walks through a quiet mango grove outside Pava, examining the trees and shaded ground where simple huts and a resting platform stand ready.

dialogue.text: Cunda also owned a mango grove beyond the palisade. It was here, in this quiet place, that his work would touch the final days of a wandering Samana from the Sakyan clan.

i18n.hi: कुंडा के पास नगर घेरे के बाहर एक आम्रबट भी था। इसी शांति भरे बाग में उसका काम शाक्य कुल के एक भटकते सामन के अंतिम दिनों से जुड़ने वाला था।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a newly-built assembly hall with wooden pillars and benches
panels.action: Inside the freshly completed Ubbhataka assembly hall, Malla clansmen sit on benches, wooden pillars rising around them, as elders confer at the center with grave attention.

dialogue.text: In those days, the Mallas of Pava had just raised a new santhagara, the Ubbhataka hall. Here they met as equals, debated, and settled matters of war, peace, and law.

i18n.hi: तभी पावा के मल्लों ने नया संथागार खड़ा किया था—उब्भटक सभा भवन। यहीं वे बराबरी से बैठते, बहस करते, और युद्ध, शांति व नियमों के फैसले बाँटते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Malla elders in discussion, one gesturing toward the doorway
panels.action: Several Malla elders, wrapped in plain upper garments, sit facing one another; one points toward the open doorway where daylight pours in, hinting at decisions about visitors and affairs beyond.

dialogue.text: The Mahaparinibbana Sutta remembers this hall by name. While kings ruled elsewhere, here a republic framed its choices in counsel, even as a greater story unfolded nearby.

i18n.hi: महापरिनिब्बान सुत्त इस सभा भवन को नाम लेकर याद करता है। जहाँ औरों पर राजा राज करते थे, वहाँ यह गण अपने फैसले परामर्श से गढ़ रहा था, जबकि पास ही एक बड़ा प्रसंग चल रहा था।

panels.shot: low-angle long shot of the Buddha and monks approaching Pava along a dusty road
panels.action: A serene ascetic leader walks at the head of a small band of monks along a dusty road toward Pava, staff in hand, robes gathered, as villagers watch from the roadside.

dialogue.text: From the west, the Buddha came toward Pava, nearing the end of a long ministry. The text places him here, at the edge of the Mallas’ town, as his last journey turned toward Kusinara.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम से बुद्ध पावा की ओर आए, अपने लंबे धर्मयात्रा के अंत के क़रीब। ग्रंथ उन्हें यहीं ठहराता है, मल्ल नगर की सीमा पर, जब उनकी आख़िरी डगर कुसीनारा की ओर मुड़ती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Cunda hurrying from the forge toward the grove, tools set aside
panels.action: Cunda wipes soot from his arms, quickly sets his hammer aside, and strides from his workshop toward the path leading to his mango grove, resolve clear in his face.

dialogue.text: Hearing that the Buddha had arrived, Cunda invited him to stay in his mango grove. For a kammara, this was no small act—it meant turning a workplace into a refuge.

i18n.hi: बुद्ध के आने की ख़बर सुनकर कुंडा ने उन्हें अपने आम्रबट में ठहरने का निमंत्रण दिया। एक कम्मार के लिए यह छोटी बात न थी—काम की जगह को ही आश्रय में बदल देना था।

panels.shot: medium shot at the grove entrance, Cunda bowing before the Teacher (shown only from behind) and monks
panels.action: At the entrance of the mango grove, Cunda bows deeply, palms joined, before the calm figure of the Teacher and the line of monks standing with alms-bowls in hand.

dialogue.speaker: Cunda of Pava
dialogue.text: Venerable Sir, may this grove and my offering be yours tonight.

i18n.hi: भगवन्, यह बगिया और मेरी भेंट, आज रात आपकी हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of a simple outdoor kitchen in the grove, Cunda overseeing pots
panels.action: Cunda stands beside makeshift hearths under the mango trees, directing helpers as they tend steaming pots and arrange simple dishes on low platforms.

dialogue.text: The Sutta tells of the meal prepared there. Cunda arranged various foods and a dish called sukaramaddava. Its exact nature is lost to us; tradition has offered many guesses, the text offers none.

i18n.hi: सुत्त वहाँ तैयार भोजन का वर्णन करता है। कुंडा ने कई व्यंजन और सुकरमद्दव नाम का पकवान सजाया। उसका रूप अब खो गया; परंपरा ने कई अटकलें लगाईं, खुद पाठ चुप रहता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Cunda respectfully presenting bowls of food to the Teacher seated under a tree
panels.action: Seated under a spreading mango tree, the Teacher receives a bowl from Cunda, who kneels with lowered gaze and steady hands, other monks seated quietly beyond.

dialogue.text: The Buddha accepted Cunda’s offering. The Mahaparinibbana Sutta remembers this meal clearly, for it was his last before he walked on toward Kusinara.

i18n.hi: बुद्ध ने कुंडा की भेंट स्वीकार की। महापरिनिब्बान सुत्त इस भोजन को साफ़-साफ़ याद रखता है, क्योंकि कुसीनारा की ओर चलने से पहले यह उनका अंतिम आहार था।

panels.shot: close-up on Cunda’s thoughtful face that night in the grove, firelight flickering
panels.action: Night has fallen; Cunda sits near a small fire in the grove, his face lit by flames, eyes troubled as he gazes at the dark path leading away from Pava.

dialogue.text: Later, when the Teacher fell ill and his passing drew near, Cunda’s simple act weighed heavily in rumor and in his own mind. The text records his anxiety with unusual care.

i18n.hi: बाद में, जब शिक्षक अस्वस्थ पड़े और उनका अंत निकट आया, कुंडा की साधारण भेंट अफ़वाहों और उसके अपने मन पर भारी पड़ने लगी। पाठ उसकी चिंता को असाधारण सावधानी से दर्ज करता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Buddha and Ananda walking away from Pava toward Kusinara at dawn
panels.action: At dawn, the Teacher walks with his attendant along a quiet countryside path, the town of Pava shrinking behind them as light breaks over fields and trees.

dialogue.text: From Cunda’s grove the Buddha went on, toward a sal grove near Kusinara, where he would attain parinibbana. But Pava stayed behind in the story, holding this fragile thread of memory.

i18n.hi: कुंडा की बगिया से बुद्ध आगे बढ़े, कुसीनारा के पास एक साल वृक्षों की बगिया की ओर, जहाँ वे परिनिब्बान को प्राप्त होंगे। पर कहानी में पावा यहीं रुक जाता है, स्मृति की यह नाज़ुक डोर थामे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ananda listening closely to the Buddha, suggested by posture and gesture
panels.action: On the road, the Teacher speaks gently to his attendant, who listens with joined palms and lowered head, the landscape stretching empty around them.

dialogue.text: The Sutta preserves a set of instructions given to protect Cunda. The Buddha told his attendant that Cunda should feel no remorse, that he should be told he had made a great, twofold offering.

i18n.hi: सुत्त कुंडा की रक्षा के लिए दिए गए निर्देश भी सहेज कर रखता है। बुद्ध ने अपने सेवक से कहा कि कुंडा को कोई ग्लानि न हो, उसे बताया जाए कि उसने महान, द्वि-युक्ति भेंट दी है।

panels.shot: symbolic split-frame: one side shows the first alms-meal after enlightenment, the other Cunda’s offering
panels.action: A stylized composition shows, on one side, a vision of the Buddha’s first alms-meal after awakening; on the other, Cunda’s meal in the mango grove, both framed in equal, balanced panels.

dialogue.text: He taught that two offerings stand unmatched: the meal served before enlightenment at Uruvela, and Cunda’s meal before parinibbana. Thus the text itself lifts Cunda from suspicion to honor.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने सिखाया कि दो भेंटें अनुपम हैं—उरुवेला में बोधि से पहले का भोजन, और परिनिब्बान से पहले कुंडा का भोजन। इस तरह खुद पाठ कुंडा को शक से सम्मान तक उठा देता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a messenger monk speaking to Cunda in the grove, both seated
panels.action: Back in the mango grove, Cunda sits across from a monk-messenger who speaks calmly, hands open, while Cunda’s expression begins to soften from worry to quiet relief.

dialogue.text: So the message was to reach Cunda in Pava: that he bore no blame, that his act would be remembered as meritorious, not as cause of death. The textual voice is careful, almost protective.

i18n.hi: तो पावा में कुंडा तक यह खबर पहुँचनी थी—कि उस पर कोई दोष नहीं, उसका कर्म पुण्य समझा जाएगा, मृत्यु का कारण नहीं। पाठ की आवाज़ यहाँ नर्म है, मानो उसे ढाँपती हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of Cunda standing outside the Ubbhataka hall, looking from the hall up to the open sky
panels.action: Cunda stands near the Ubbhataka assembly hall, watching Malla citizens disperse while he lifts his gaze to the open sky, the grove visible in the distance.

dialogue.text: Cunda’s story ends quietly in the sources. He returns to his tools, his grove, his republic. But the Malla hall and his name stay bound together in this brief meeting with a passing Samana.

i18n.hi: कुंडा की कथा स्रोतों में चुपचाप थम जाती है। वह अपने औज़ारों, अपनी बगिया, अपने गण में लौट जाता है। पर मल्ल सभा भवन और उसका नाम, उस गुजरते सामन से हुई इस छोटी भेंट में हमेशा के लिए बँध जाते हैं।

panels.shot: aerial pullback from Pava’s hall and grove to the wider landscape of ancient republics and kingdoms
panels.action: The view pulls back to show Pava’s Ubbhataka hall and Cunda’s mango grove as small features within a broad landscape of towns, rivers, and forests fading into distance.

dialogue.text: Through one blacksmith’s offering and one named hall, the Mahaparinibbana Sutta lets a small republic step from the shadows—reminding us how often great changes brush the lives of ordinary hands.

i18n.hi: एक लोहार की भेंट और एक सभा भवन के ज़रिए, महापरिनिब्बान सुत्त एक छोटे गणराज्य को परछाइयों से बाहर रखता है—याद दिलाते हुए कि बड़े बदलाव अक्सर साधारण हाथों को हल्के से छू कर गुजर जाते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: A meal in a mango grove, a hall of citizens, and the last walk of a teacher
subtitle_i18n.hi: आमों की बगिया में भोजन, नागरिकों का सभा भवन, और गुरु की आख़िरी डगर
